newsitem.title: CHINA: China central bank sets rules on cash withdrawals.
newsitem.headline: China central bank sets rules on cash withdrawals.

text.p: China's central bank has set new rules allowing it to monitor large cash withdrawals from the nation's banks in a bid to curb economic crime, the Financial News said on Thursday.

It said that "unreasonably large" cash withdrawals from commercial banks and credit cooperatives would have to be recorded and reported to the local branch of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The size of cash withdrawals that would have to be reported would be determined by the local central bank branch according to local financial requirements.
The new regulations would not be aimed at individuals but rather at all enterprises and other economic organisations, including foreign companies.

All banks and credit cooperatives would have to establish a monitoring system by July 1. Once the system was in place, all large cash withdrawals would have to be reported to the central bank within 15 days. China has been trying to curb a sharp rise in economic crime that has accompanied rapid economic growth.
The newspaper did not name any specific crimes but illegal payments to officials, usually made in cash, have been a particular problem in China.
